I kept **2638 of 2700 cells and 13714 genes**. I found **7 clusters** at the recorded Leiden resolution of 0.7, with 10 neighbors, 40 principal components and seed 0. The cluster count depends on the resolution. Six clusters match known blood cell types by their marker genes. One large cluster has no clear marker.

## Cleaning steps
1. **Load data:** 2700 cells and 32738 genes, as raw counts. The data are one sample from one donor.
2. **Filter genes:** I kept genes found in at least 3 cells. Genes went from 32738 to 13714, which is 41.9 % (calculate step).
3. **QC metrics:** the human mitochondrial prefix MT- matched 13 genes. The QC violin plot is `calculate_qc-1/qc_violin.png` and the quantiles are in `qc_quantiles.csv`.

   | Metric | Min | Median | 95th percentile | 99th percentile | Max |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | Genes per cell | 212 | 816 | 1368 | 1739 | 3400 |
   | Counts per cell | 546 | 2196 | – | – | 15818 |
   | Percent mitochondrial counts | 0 | 2.03 | 4.01 | 5.88 | 22.57 |

4. **Filter cells:** the recorded cutoffs were at least 200 genes, fewer than 2500 genes and less than 5 % mitochondrial counts.
   * Cells went from 2700 to 2638, which is 97.7 % (calculate step).
   * No cell had too few genes.
   * 5 cells had too many genes.
   * 57 cells had too much mitochondrial RNA.
   * These cutoffs are the same as the standard scanpy 3k blood cell tutorial (PBMC = peripheral blood mononuclear cells). The harness recorded them as your decisions.
5. **Rest of the cleaning:**
   * Each cell was scaled to 10000 counts, then log-transformed.
   * The cutoff method (not a fixed number of genes) marked 1838 highly variable genes.
   * The scaling step removed the effect of total counts and percent mitochondrial counts.
   * PCA (principal component analysis) computed 50 components with seed 0.

## Clusters
At resolution 0.7 (`cluster_leiden-5/leiden.h5ad`), the 7 clusters hold 1174, 486, 438, 341, 150, 36 and 13 cells.

How the count changes with the resolution (comparison runs only; the record still says 0.7):

| Resolution | Clusters | Smallest cluster | Largest cluster |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 5 | 13 | 1239 |
| 0.5 | 6 | 13 | 1195 |
| 0.7 | 7 | 13 | 1174 |
| 1.0 | 8 | 13 | 1138 |
| 1.5 | 14 | 13 | 429 |

The 13-cell cluster appears at every resolution. The total number of clusters depends on the resolution.

## Marker genes for each cluster
I used the Wilcoxon test, from the find_markers step. "LFC" is the log2 fold change of a cluster against all other cells, and p.adj is the adjusted p-value. These p-values are only descriptive, because the same cells made the clusters and the test. The full top 25 lists are in `find_markers-1/markers.csv`.

| Cluster (cells) | Top genes (LFC, p.adj) | Known markers that support a name | Putative cell type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (1174) | RPS12 (1.06, 2.7e-226), LDHB (2.72, 2.1e-223), RPS25 (1.18, 1.1e-200), RPS27, RPS6 | Only CD3D (rank 8, LFC 3.24). IL7R, CCR7, CD8A and CD8B are not in the top 25. | Putative T cells, probably a mix of CD4 and CD8 T cells |
| 1 (341) | CD74 (4.08, 3.4e-179), CD79A (7.75, 1.2e-166), HLA-DRA (4.89, 3.2e-163), CD79B (5.52, 8.8e-151), HLA-DPB1 | CD79A (rank 2) and MS4A1 (rank 6, LFC 6.43) | B cells |
| 2 (486) | LYZ (6.24, 1.4e-248), S100A9 (7.35, 2.5e-244), S100A8 (7.58, 4.3e-235), TYROBP (5.51, 7.6e-221), FTL | LYZ (rank 1). CD14 is not in the top 25. | Putative CD14 monocytes |
| 3 (438) | NKG7 (7.06, 8.5e-213), CST7 (6.41, 4.5e-170), GZMA (6.09, 2.0e-159), B2M (0.98, 1.7e-157), CTSW (4.64, 4.5e-155) | NKG7 (rank 1), GZMB (rank 14), GNLY (rank 17, LFC 5.06) | NK cells, probably mixed with cytotoxic T cells (CCL5 and GZMH are also present) |
| 4 (150) | LST1 (5.18, 7.8e-81), FCER1G (4.79, 1.2e-77), AIF1 (4.82, 6.3e-76), COTL1 (3.61, 3.3e-74), FCGR3A (5.57, 6.9e-73) | FCGR3A (rank 5) and MS4A7 (rank 25, LFC 4.99) | FCGR3A monocytes |
| 5 (36) | HLA-DPA1 (4.28, 5.2e-17), HLA-DPB1 (4.43, 5.2e-17), HLA-DRA (4.61, 6.0e-16), HLA-DRB1 (4.24, 6.4e-16), CD74 (3.64, 1.3e-15) | FCER1A (rank 8, LFC 8.77), CST3 (rank 7), CLEC10A | Dendritic cells |
| 6 (13) | PF4 (12.91, 7.7e-07), GNG11 (12.43, 7.7e-07), SDPR (11.86, 7.7e-07), PPBP (13.04, 7.7e-07), NRGN (9.09, 7.7e-07) | PPBP (rank 4), PF4 (rank 1) | Megakaryocytes (platelets) |

## What is uncertain
* **Cluster 0 is the largest cluster (1174 cells), but ribosomal genes lead its marker list.** The CD4 markers (IL7R, CCR7) and CD8 markers (CD8A, CD8B) are not in its top 25. So it is probably a mix of CD4 and CD8 T cells that this resolution does not split.
* **Cluster 3 can hold NK cells and cytotoxic T cells together.**
* **I could not check how many cells in each cluster express each known marker.** The script environment cannot read .h5ad files. The dot plot `plot_genes-1/genes_dotplot.png` shows these values, but I did not read the image. You must look at it to confirm the names.
* **The number of components is high for this curve.** The PCA variance drops after PC4 and is almost flat after PC10, but the recorded choice is 40 components. A smaller number can change the clusters.
* **Cluster 6 holds only 13 cells.** Its adjusted p-values are therefore much weaker (7.7e-07) than those of the other clusters.
* **This is one sample from one donor.** No comparison between conditions is possible, and the cells are not independent replicates.

## What waits for you
* Look at the QC violin plot, the PCA variance plot `run_pca-1/pca_variance.png` and the dot plot.
* Decide if resolution 0.7 is right. A higher resolution can split cluster 0 into CD4 and CD8 T cells. The comparison runs gave 8 clusters at 1.0 and 14 at 1.5.
* Decide if 40 components is right, given the elbow near PC4 to PC10.

The final checkpoint is `find_markers-1/markers.h5ad`, with the clusters stored in `cluster_leiden-5/leiden.h5ad`.

## Cells and genes kept
1. **Load (load_data):** 2700 cells and 32738 genes, as raw counts.
2. **Gene filter (filter_genes):** a gene must occur in at least 3 cells. 13714 genes stay and 19024 go.
3. **QC metrics (calculate_qc):** human mitochondrial genes, prefix MT-, 13 genes.
   - Genes per cell: median 816, maximum 3400.

   - Minimum genes per cell: 200 (min_genes=200).
   - Maximum genes per cell: fewer than 2500.
   - Maximum mitochondrial counts: less than 5 percent.
   - Removed: 0 cells for too few genes, 5 for too many genes, 57 for high mitochondrial counts.
   - **Result: 2638 cells × 13714 genes.**

These are the cutoffs you entered. They are the same as the standard scanpy blood-cell tutorial for this data set. I did not change them.

## Steps before clustering
- **Normalization (normalize_log):** each cell is scaled to 10000 counts, then log1p is applied.
- **Variable genes (find_variable_genes):** 1838 genes, found with the mean and dispersion cutoffs.
- **Scaling (scale_data):** total counts and percent mitochondrial counts are regressed out. Values are clipped at 10.
- **Principal component analysis (run_pca):** 50 components.

## Clusters (chosen settings)
- **Settings:** Leiden resolution 0.7, 10 neighbors, 40 components, random seed 0.
- **Result (cluster_leiden):** 7 clusters with 1174, 486, 438, 341, 150, 36 and 13 cells.
- The UMAP plot is `run_umap-1/umap.png`.

**Sensitivity check:** these numbers come from comparison runs (compare_options), not from the chosen setting. They only show how the count changes. Seed 0 was the same in all runs.

| Resolution | Clusters | Largest cluster (cells) | Smallest cluster (cells) |

## Marker genes of each cluster
- **Test (find_markers):** Wilcoxon, which compares each cluster with all other cells.

| 3 (438) | NKG7 (7.06, 8.5e-213), CST7 (6.41), GZMA (6.09), B2M (0.98), CTSW (4.64) | NKG7 (1), GZMB (14), GNLY (17; LFC 5.06, padj 5.6e-51), PRF1 | NK cells, possibly mixed with CD8 T cells |
| 4 (150) | LST1 (5.18, 7.8e-81), FCER1G (4.79), AIF1 (4.82), COTL1 (3.61), FCGR3A (5.57, 6.9e-73) | FCGR3A (5), MS4A7 (25; LFC 4.99) | FCGR3A monocytes |
| 5 (36) | HLA-DPA1 (4.28, 5.2e-17), HLA-DPB1 (4.43), HLA-DRA (4.61), HLA-DRB1 (4.24), CD74 (3.64) | CST3 (7), FCER1A (8; LFC 8.77, padj 2.1e-14), CLEC10A | Dendritic cells |
| 6 (13) | PF4 (12.9), GNG11 (12.4), SDPR (11.9), PPBP (13.0), NRGN (9.09), all padj 7.7e-7 | PPBP (4) | Putative megakaryocytes (platelets) |

The full lists are in `find_markers-1/markers.csv` and `canonical_genes_in_marker_lists.csv`. The canonical-marker dot plot is `plot_genes-1/genes_dotplot.png`.

## Uncertainties
- **No CD4/CD8 split:** IL7R, CCR7, CD8A and CD8B are not in the top 25 genes of any cluster.
  - Cluster 0 probably holds CD4 T cells, and possibly some CD8 T cells. Ribosomal genes lead its marker list.
  - Cluster 3 has CCL5, IL32 and CD247, so it can hold CD8 T cells as well as NK cells.
  - In the comparison runs, higher resolutions made the largest cluster smaller. This suggests that cluster 0 splits. I did not test markers at those resolutions.
- **Dot plot values:** I could not read the per-cluster values of the dot plot as numbers, because the script cannot open the checkpoint (the anndata module is missing). The cell-type names rest only on the ranked marker lists.
- **Number of components:** the variance curve (run_pca) is almost flat after about PC10, but the graph uses 40 components. I did not test fewer components, so I do not know whether this changes the clusters.
- **Small clusters:** clusters 5 (36 cells) and 6 (13 cells) are small. Their p-values are much weaker than those of the large clusters.

## Waiting for you
- Do you want CD4 and CD8 T cells as separate clusters? If yes, choose a higher resolution, and I will repeat the marker step.
- Do you want to check the effect of fewer principal components? If yes, change the n_pcs decision.

The final checkpoint is `find_markers-1/markers.h5ad`.

I kept **2638 of 2700 cells** (97.7 %) and found **7 clusters** at the recorded resolution of 0.7. The number of clusters depends on the resolution, so 7 is the result for this one setting only.

## What I did
I used the standard Scanpy steps with your recorded settings:
1. **Load** (load_data): 2700 cells and 32738 genes, raw counts.
2. **Gene filter** (filter_genes, at least 3 cells per gene): 13714 of 32738 genes kept (41.9 %).
3. **Quality control** (calculate_qc, mitochondrial prefix MT-):
   - Genes per cell: median 816, maximum 3400.
   - Counts per cell: median 2196.
   - Percent mitochondrial counts: median 2.03, maximum 22.57.
   - The violin plot is `calculate_qc-1/qc_violin.png`. The quantile table is `qc_quantiles.csv`.
4. **Cell filter** (filter_cells: min_genes 200, max_genes 2500, max_pct_mito 5): 2638 of 2700 cells kept, 62 removed (2.3 %).
   - 0 cells for too few genes.
   - 5 cells for too many genes.
   - 57 cells for high mitochondrial counts.
5. **Normalization** (normalize_log): each cell scaled to 10000 counts, then log1p.
6. **Variable genes** (find_variable_genes): 1838 highly variable genes, with the mean and dispersion cutoffs.
7. **Scaling** (scale_data): total_counts and pct_counts_mt regressed out, values clipped at 10.
8. **Principal component analysis** (run_pca): 50 components. The first 10 hold 6.4 % of the variance. The variance plot has an elbow after PC 4 to 5.
9. **Clustering**: the neighbor graph used 10 neighbors and 40 components. Then I ran the UMAP (a 2D map of the cells) and Leiden clustering at resolution 0.7. The random seed was 0 in all steps.

## Number of clusters
**Result** (cluster_leiden, resolution 0.7): 7 clusters. Their sizes are 1174, 486, 438, 341, 150, 36 and 13 cells.

**Sensitivity check only.** These numbers come from comparison runs, not from the chosen setting. The runs used the same neighbors, components and seed. The record still says 0.7.

| **Chosen, 0.7** | **7** | **1174** | **13** |
| Comparison run, 1 | 8 | 1138 | 13 |
| Comparison run, 1.5 | 14 | 429 | 13 |

In this check, a cluster of 13 cells is present at every resolution. The cluster count changes with the resolution.

## Marker genes
The test was Wilcoxon, each cluster against all other cells (find_markers, chosen resolution 0.7). LFC is the log fold change. Adjusted p is the adjusted p-value. All p-values are **descriptive**. The clusters come from the same cells that the test ranks, so the p-values do not test a hypothesis.

- **Cluster 0 mixes T cells.** CD4 and CD8 T cells do not separate at resolution 0.7. Its top genes are mostly ribosomal genes, and the T cell label rests on CD3D and LDHB only. That is why the label says "putative".

- **The data hold one sample from one donor.** These results describe one sample only. You cannot compare conditions or compute p-values between groups with these data.

## What waits for you

- **Number of components:** the record uses 40. The variance plot flattens after about PC 10, so you can check this choice.
- **QC cutoffs:** please confirm that the cutoffs in the record fit this tissue and chemistry.
